rationale: Job asks whether the Lord hears the distressed ungodly person's plea; Elihu later describes cries not heard because of evil people's insolence.

Job pictures his former roads and mountains flooded with butter and milk; Zophar had denied the ungodly person the milking of herds and pastures of honey and butter. The figurative and stated details are preserved.
Job says God regards him as clay and assigns him earth and ashes; his earlier appeal recalled being molded as clay and turned back to earth.

Job's conditional oath about walking with mockers and hastening toward deceit accords with his prior commitment that his lips and soul would not produce lawless or unjust things. The conditional form is retained.

relationship: Claiming attachment to God does not establish wisdom
rationale: Elihu rejects the friends' claim to have found wisdom by attaching themselves to the Lord; Job had warned that attaching themselves to Him would not prevent divine reproof for partiality.

relationship: Drinking moral wrongdoing as a rhetorical image
rationale: Elihu accuses Job of drinking mockery like water; Eliphaz had pictured the unclean man drinking injustice as a drink. The different objects of drinking and the speakers' accusations are preserved.

The proposed appeal asks God to show what the speaker has not seen and promises not to add to injustice; Job had already asked to be taught his sins and lawless deeds. Elihu's proposal is not presented as a request Job had never made.
